semantics.note: An observation that multimodal models still hallucinate. Dropping 'magically' is acceptable. The claim says nothing about improvement or impossibility, and the contract correctly reads it as persistence, not as no progress.

contract.note: Reading the claim as 'contemporary multimodal models still hallucinate' is the ordinary meaning and is not stretched either way. Lower error rates alone do not count against it, which is fair.

evidence.note: OpenAI's GPT-4V system card from Sept 2023, published before the post. It says the model was prone to hallucinations. This is the company disclosing a limitation of its own model, so it is not an independent finding. The packet lists it as counterevidence because it mentions reductions, but reduction is not elimination.
Independent preprint from May 2023, before the post. It found severe object hallucination in several representative vision-language models, which supports persistence after multimodal training.

reviews.rationale: Both pre-publication sources show multimodal models still hallucinating in 2023: an independent systematic study (e2) and OpenAI's own GPT-4V disclosure (e1). The reported reductions in hallucination do not show elimination, so the claim holds as an observation of the period.
